# Testing and verification

## Use the preconfigured Linux CLI

Run `scripts/setup-linux-playwright.sh` on an Ubuntu worker to install the pinned
CLI, Chromium, Mesa Vulkan drivers, and a persistent Xvfb display. Let the reusable
workflow run this before publishing SSH access. Use `playwright-cli` from Actions
or a fresh SSH shell; let the wrapper supply DISPLAY and the Linux configuration.
Use `playwright-cli -s=check open <url>`, `eval`, `screenshot`, and `close` without
manual browser flags. Load `.github/templates/linux.md` by default. Select `mac.md` instead when
a `mac` label or `#mac` hashtag is present. Match case insensitively. Recheck the actual screenshot after upgrades.

## Capture the Linux WebGPU triangle

Install Playwright 1.63.0 and its full Chromium browser as below. Install
`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `vulkan-tools`, and `xvfb` on Ubuntu. Serve
`tests/fixtures/webgpu-triangle.html` over localhost HTTP. Run:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-runtime xvfb-run -a node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/webgpu-triangle.html --canvas '#wgpu' \
  --backend swiftshader --require-green-triangle --out /tmp/linux-triangle
```

Require green triangle pixels, a usable device, `scene.webgpu.rendered=true`,
and no page errors. Inspect the image. Treat SwiftShader and Mesa llvmpipe as
CPU rendering, not GPU hardware acceleration. Use the headed Xvfb result on
[run 34908797646](https://github.com/AgentsLoop/PlayGround/actions/runs/34908797646)
as the verified 2026-09-15 reference. Do not accept the headless result from
that run: its initial generic pixel check falsely accepted background pixels.
Retain the fixture's GPU reference. Preserve failed diagnostics when investigating
`A valid external Instance reference no longer exists`. Do not infer a single
root cause from the combined driver-installation and fixture changes.
Use `--backend vulkan` for native-driver experiments, `--backend swangle` for
ANGLE SwiftShader experiments, and `--executable` to select another browser.
Keep the default Metal path for the Mac test.

## Capture Pascal Editor on Linux

Use `http://localhost:3002`, not the numeric loopback origin, with the default
Pascal Next.js development server. Check the server log for blocked development
resources when HTTP 403 or HMR handshake errors occur.
Install dependencies with the repository's Bun lockfile. Start `bun dev` and
wait for the editor on port 3002. Create a studio through `POST /api/scenes`
using the documented scene structure. Open `/scene/<id>?disable=postFx` for
the reduced-effects capture. Do not use the empty root page as a scene test.
Run headed Chromium under Xvfb with the tested SwiftShader flags above.
Wait for visible geometry; verify the existing canvas accepts `webgpu` and
rejects `webgl2`. Require the viewer's `WebGPU device ready` log, no failed
HTTP requests, and no JavaScript errors. Inspect the screenshot manually.
Treat the 2026-09-15 room capture on issue 113 as a software-rendering result.
Do not claim full post-processing coverage. Preserve readiness-timeout warnings
in the report; do not confuse an earlier WebGL fallback capture with the final
WebGPU capture. Keep the saved scene and application server for further tests.

## Capture WebGPU on a hosted Mac

Use full Chromium with the Metal backend. Keep Playwright's other launch defaults. Test
headed mode first; use `--headless` only after comparing the actual captures.
Install Playwright and its full Chromium build in a separate runtime directory:

```sh
npm install --prefix /tmp/gpu-capture-runtime playwright@1.63.0
/tmp/gpu-capture-runtime/node_modules/.bin/playwright install chromium
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-capture-runtime node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/ --canvas '#wgpu' \
  --require-metal --out /tmp/game-capture
```

Replace the URL and canvas selector with the running game's values. Start the
game before capture if it requires user input. Read `diagnostic.json`,
`canvas.png`, and `page.png` from the output directory. Require an available
WebGPU device, no page errors, and painted canvas pixels. Exclude CSS borders
from the pixel check. Accept a flat triangle with two interior colours; reject
a uniform interior even when its border has another colour.

Use `--baseline` to test full Chromium without extra flags. Use `--headless`
to test the same full browser headlessly. Do not substitute the separate
headless shell. Preserve failed diagnostics; do not silently skip absent
adapters. Keep Vulkan flags out of the macOS Metal capture path.

Use the verified flags: `--enable-gpu`, `--ignore-gpu-blocklist`,
`--enable-unsafe-webgpu`, and `--use-angle=metal`. Check `chrome://gpu` in a
separate headed page. Interpret `Apple Paravirtual device` as a virtual Metal
adapter, not proof of a physical GPU model or hardware performance.

Refer to [Playwright's browser documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers#opt-in-to-new-headless-mode)
for the full-browser/headless-shell distinction. Reproduce the evidence from
[issue #110](https://github.com/AgentsLoop/PlayGround/issues/110) and
[run 34801504801](https://github.com/AgentsLoop/PlayGround/actions/runs/34801504801).
Use the 2026-09-14 result as a reference, not a promise for later runner images:
Playwright 1.63.0 / Chromium 153.0.8010.12 acquired vendor `apple`,
`isFallbackAdapter=false`, and a usable WebGPU device. Both headed and headless
Metal captures visibly showed the green triangle; pure headed baseline also
succeeded. Run `node --test scripts/gpu-capture.test.mjs` for the pixel and
symlink-entry regressions, then repeat the live screenshot test.

## Test standalone issue access

Create an issue with the `OpenCode` label and `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone`.
Verify that Actions starts one execution job.
Restore the access variable after testing. Verify restricted access with the
variable unset. Verify one Actions run for each new issue.

## Test the `-rc` repository at a selected commit

Use the release-candidate repository when you need to test the workflow against
an older or experimental commit without changing the source repository.

Set the repository and commit variables first:

```sh
repo=denaidark/OhMyGithub-rc
commit=<full-commit-sha>
branch=rc-<short-commit-sha>
```

Create a branch from the exact commit and make it the GitHub default branch:

```sh
git push "https://github.com/$repo.git" "${commit}:refs/heads/$branch"
gh repo edit "$repo" --default-branch "$branch"
gh repo view "$repo" --json defaultBranchRef
```

Keep the existing `main` branch and older test branches. Use a new branch name
for each commit so the tested revision remains clear and recoverable. The
workflow checks out the GitHub default branch when the issue title has no
branch metadata.

Create an SSH test issue with the required labels:

```sh
gh issue create --repo "$repo" \
  --title "Check SSH connectivity on $branch" \
  --body $'# Check SSH connectivity on <branch>\n\nVerify the temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, authentication, tunnel, and remote response. Record concrete evidence without exposing secrets.' \

function calcDamage(attacker, defender, move, rng=Math.random) {
 if (!move.power) return 0;
 const atk = attacker.atk * stageMult(attacker.stages.atk) * (attacker.status==='burn'?0.5:1);
 const def = defender.def * stageMult(defender.stages.def);
 const crit = rng() < 1/16;
 let dmg = Math.floor((((2*attacker.level/5+2)*move.power*atk/def)/50+2));
 if (crit) dmg = Math.floor(dmg*1.5);
 if (attacker.type === move.type) dmg = Math.floor(dmg*1.5);
 const eff = typeEffect(move.type, defender.type);
 dmg = Math.floor(dmg*eff);
 dmg = Math.max(1, Math.floor(dmg*(0.85+rng()*0.15)));
 return {damage:dmg, crit, effectiveness:eff};
}
```

Turn resolution:

```js
function resolveTurn(state, action, rng=Math.random) {
  const events=[]
  if (state.over) return events
  const p = playerMon(state), e = enemyMon(state)
  if (!p || p.fainted) { ... requestSwitch }
  if (action.type==='switch') { doSwitch; enemy attack; endTurn; return }
  if (action.type==='item') ...
  if (action.type==='run') ...
  if (action.type==='move') ...
  ...
  finishTurn(state, events, rng)
  return events
}
```

For item ball, catch attempt; if fail, enemy attacks. For healing item, heal then enemy attacks. For invalid (full HP) event text and return without enemy action (UI prevents). For ball trainer, text and return.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game matching the prompt "Create pokemon in a jamaican setting" in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`.

## Requirements
- User request is only the single line "Create pokemon in a jamaican setting".
- Must run as a static site from repo root (no `package.json`, because the runtime launcher rejects unsupported package projects).
- Must be mobile-friendly and visually verified in a browser via `playwright-cli` before claiming success.
- Avoid external runtime dependencies/CDNs; all art/audio should be procedural/local.

## Decisions
- Game concept: **"YAADMON: Island Spirits"** — original creature-collecting RPG set in Sweetwater Bay, Jamaica, with original species inspired by island culture (Pimenta, Turtide, Ackee, Yardgoat, Mongoose, Seacow, Cockpit, Anancy, Rolling Calf, River Mumma, Peenie Wallie, Moko Jumbie, Dr. Bird).
- Vanilla JS classic scripts sharing `window.YD` namespace; no build step.
- Canvas 2D pixel art generated procedurally; title/battle scenes animated; DOM UI for HUD/dialogue/battle/menus.
- Battle engine is pure and Node-testable; map layout is pure and BFS-testable.
- Core loop: choose starter on title → explore tile world → catch/level creatures in tall grass → defeat 3 Wardens (Fern/Finn/Zeph) → catch or defeat legendary Dr. Bird at Blue Mountain Peak → ending.
- Start screen has exactly one button labeled "Start" (matches capture automation); Continue appears only with save.
- Sound is procedural WebAudio reggae/ska loops plus SFX, with mute persistence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project structure and all game data: `js/data.js` (types, type chart, 16 species, 26+ moves, items, trainers, encounters, story).
- Pure battle engine: `js/engine.js` (stats, damage, status, AI, catching, XP/level/evolution, turn resolution, forced switches, healing).
- Pure island layout: `js/map.js` (60×44 map, roads, river/bridge, pier, beach, mountain trail, peak, buildings, NPCs, signs, props, collision, zones) — verified via ASCII print and BFS; all NPCs/interactables reachable.
- Art helpers + all 16 creature sprites: `js/art.js`.
- World tiles, props, buildings, people, portraits: `js/artworld.js` (fixed a leftover `yd` ReferenceError in the sand tile branch).
- Title and battle backdrops: `js/artscenes.js`.
- Procedural music/SFX: `js/audio.js`.
- World renderer with camera, depth sorting, water/grass animation: `js/world.js`.
- Full HTML shell: `index.html` (title, world HUD, dialogue, touch controls, battle screen, modal).
- Complete CSS visual system: `css/style.css`.
- Existing repo scripts `start.sh`, `capture.sh`, `startup.sh` untouched.

### Active
- Still to create: `js/battle.js` (battle UI controller processing engine events, HP bars, move/bag/team menus, ball animation, battle end callbacks).
- Still to create: `js/game.js` (boot, save/load, title starter selection, movement/collision, NPC dialogue/trainers/shop/heal, encounters, badges, legendary, quest, party/bag/dex/help/ending modals, touch/keyboard input, responsive canvas sizing, render loop, autosave).
- Still to create: tests (planned `tests/engine.test.mjs`, `tests/data.test.mjs`, `tests/map.test.mjs` using Node `require`).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `js/battle.js` implementing battle screen lifecycle and sequential event playback.
2. Create `js/game.js` tying title, world, NPCs, encounters, saves, modals, and input together.
3. Run `node --test` on engine/data/map tests; fix any logic/balance issues.
4. Start server in tmux with `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./start.sh` (port 3000).
5. Use `playwright-cli` to screenshot/verify: title, starter select, overworld, dialogue, encounter, battle, mobile 390×844; inspect PNGs with the read tool and iterate on visuals/errors.
6. Check console/page errors, mobile touch controls, save/load, badges, legendary/ending; create `screenshots/` evidence.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: full DOM shell and script load order.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: complete styling/responsive rules.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`, originally requested as "Create pokemon in a jamaican setting".
- Rename the finished game to **"Gigamon"** per the latest user request, while keeping its Jamaican island setting.

## Requirements
- Static site from repo root; no `package.json` at root (runtime launcher rejects unsupported package projects).
- No external runtime dependencies/CDNs; procedural/local art and audio.
- Mobile-friendly and visually verified in a real browser with `playwright-cli`.
- Latest user instruction: "Name the game Gigamon".
- Keep existing repo scaffolding scripts untouched.

## Decisions
- Game concept: **GIGAMON: Island Spirits** — original creature-collecting RPG set in Sweetwater Bay, Jamaica.
- Vanilla JS classic scripts sharing `window.YD`; no build step.
- Canvas 2D procedural pixel art; DOM UI for HUD/dialogue/battle/modals.
- Pure Node-testable battle engine and island map.
- Core loop: pick starter → explore → catch/level creatures → defeat Wardens Fern/Finn/Zeph → challenge/catch Dr. Bird at Blue Mountain Peak → ending.
- Title start button is exactly "Start"; Continue appears only when a valid save exists.
- Procedural WebAudio reggae/ska music + SFX; mute persistence.
- Branding globally renamed: `YAADMON`→`GIGAMON`, `Yaadmon`→`Gigamon`, `yaadmon`→`gigamon`, including save key `gigamon-save-v2` and mute storage.

## Work State
### Completed
- All prior game data/scenes/art/audio/world renderer/CSS/HTML shell.
- `js/battle.js`: full battle screen lifecycle, event playback, HP/XP/status cards, move/bag/team menus, forced switches, ball animation, catch/trainer result callbacks.
- `js/game.js`: boot, title/starter selection, save/load, grid movement/collision, NPC dialogue/trainers/shop/heal, wild encounters, badges, legendary/ending, party/bag/dex/help/quest/shop modals, touch/keyboard input, responsive canvases, autosave.
- Fixed missing IIFE invocations in `js/audio.js`, `js/art.js`, `js/artworld.js`, `js/artscenes.js`, `js/world.js` (files previously defined functions but never executed).
- Fixed `engine.makeMonster` to set `type` and `catchRate`; evolution now updates both. Catching previously produced `NaN` chance due to missing `catchRate`.
- Added beach tall-grass patches and changed `zoneAt` to prioritize town before beach so spawn reports Sweetwater Bay.
- Renamed all branding to Gigamon, including logo markup `GIGA` / `MON`, title, save keys, help/dex text.
- `tests/engine.test.mjs`, `tests/data.test.mjs`, `tests/map.test.mjs`: all 27 tests pass via `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`.
- Browser verification completed for title (desktop), world loading/continue, NPC dialogue, wild encounter, battle intro, battle menu, move menu, item use, failed catch, blackout, party modal, dex modal, help modal.
- Removed temporary `debug.html`; reverted cache-busting query strings from `index.html`.

### Active
- Continue visual/functional verification: finish help modal check, then test trainer battles, badge awards, Zeph gate/legendary/ending, mobile 390×844 layout, and remaining modals (bag/quest/shop/ending).
- Create final evidence screenshots in `screenshots/`.
- Remove or ignore remaining favicon 404 (only recurring console error).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish verifying help modal and close it; test quest ribbon, bag, market/shop, and heal interactions.
2. Inject localStorage save data to place a high-level party near Fern/Finn/Zeph and verify trainer battles, badge UI updates, Zeph gate opening, Golden Ball reward, and Dr. Bird challenge/ending.
3. Verify mobile viewport 390×844: touch d-pad/A/B, dialogue, battle, HUD responsiveness.
4. Check browser console for errors; add a favicon or suppress the 404.
5. Save representative screenshots under `screenshots/` and do a final code/test pass.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: title/world/battle/modal DOM; now branded Gigamon; final script order.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: main game shell, saves, story, NPCs, modals, input, render loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/battle.js`: battle UI controller and event playback.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/engine.js`: pure battle mechanics; includes type/catchRate fixes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/data.js`: species/moves/trainers/encounters/items/story.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/map.js`: island layout, NPC positions, zone logic, collision.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: overworld renderer.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art.js`: creature sprites and drawing helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/artworld.js`: tiles, props, buildings, people, portraits.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/artscenes.js`: title and battle backdrops.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: procedural music/SFX/mute.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: full visual system and responsive rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/engine.test.mjs`: engine tests (27 total pass with data/map).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/data.test.mjs`: data integrity tests.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/map.test.mjs`: map/BFS/reachability tests.
